newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA STEPS UP INOCULATION CONTROLS FOR E.EUROPE.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA STEPS UP INOCULATION CONTROLS FOR E.EUROPE.

text.p: Bulgaria said on Tuesday it was stepping up vaccination controls on its citizens travelling in Eastern Europe and visitors from nearby countries to prevent the spread of diseases such as diphtheria and polio.

"Bulgarians travelling to the Balkan region, CIS and the Baltic states are required to provide a document showing they have been vaccinated against certain infectious diseases," an official from the Epidemiological Inspectorate told Reuters.

The official said that under regulations approved by the Health Ministry, Bulgarian citizens who travel to Russia, other CIS countries or the Baltic states, should present proof of inoculation against tetanus and diphtheria.

Bulgarians travelling to other Balkan countries -- Greece, Turkey, Albania, Macedonia, Romania and rump Yugoslavia -- are required to provide a certificate that they have been inoculated against poliomyelitis.
"The measures, aimed at preventing a spread of the diseases in the country, apply also to foreigners permanently based in Bulgaria," the official told Reuters.
The official said foreigners from the Balkan region, the CIS countries and the Baltic states should present vaccination certificates for the same diseases when entering the country.
"The measures are made necessary by the likelihood of an epidemic of the respective diseases in those particular countries," the official said.
Preventive healthcare programmes in many former East bloc countries have fallen victim to economic decline since the collapse of Communism in 1989.
The official said polio and diphtheria had not been a problem in Bulgaria in the past decade but the country wanted to keep them out.
Bulgaria's healthcare system is desperately short of cash and the World Bank in April approved a restructuring project worth $47.1 million.
